THIS MFA FILED U/S.173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT,
1988, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 28.02.2020 PASSED IN MVC NO.14/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE III ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, DHARWAD, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF Rs.7,28,000/- WITH INTEREST AT 8 PERCENT P.A.
 THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though these appeals are listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, they are taken up for final disposal.
2. Challenging judgment and award dated 28.02.2020 passed by III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Dharwad in MVC.no.14/2017, these appeals are filed.

entities.text: Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Brief facts as stated are that on 24.03.2015 Prakash Singh, while working as cleaner in VRL bus bearing registration no.KA-25/D-4790 traveling from Mumbai to Bijapur met with accident near Mauja Dahivali village when it dashed against a tree.
In said accident, Prakash Singh sustained grievous injuries.
Though, he was admitted to hospital for treatment he died on 27.03.2015.
4. Alleging loss of dependency on account of his untimely death, his elder brother Rajendra Singh filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, against owner and insurer of VRL bus.
5. On service of summons, respondents - owner and insurer entered appearance and filed objections.
Owner in its objections disputed only liability to pay compensation on ground that vehicle was insured with insurer and policy was valid as on date of accident.

Insurer filed objections alleging that at time of accident, vehicle was carrying excessive passengers and there was violation of policy conditions as driver did not have valid and effective driving licence and vehicle did not have permit and fitness certificate.
It also denied Prakash Singh was employee of insured.
6. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and thereafter, recorded evidence of claimant as PW.1.
It got marked Exhibits P1 to P16.

On other hand, insurer did not lead oral evidence, it got marked copy of insurance policy with consent as Ex.R1.
7.
On consideration, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver, vehicle was covered under insurance policy and valid as on date of accident.

Therefore, insurer was liable to pay compensation assessed it by at Rs.7,28,000/- with interest at The Divisional Manager vs Rajendra Singh on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74304366/
3 rate of 8% per annum.
8.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by quantum of compensation as regards dependency insurer is in appeal.
While claimant has filed appeal for enhancement of compensation.

9. Sri M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel for insurer submitted that claimant was non-dependent elder brother of deceased Prakash Singh, who was married and living separately as admitted during cross- examination and therefore would not be a dependent.
Hence, claim petition was liable for dismissal.
It was also submitted that award of interest at rate of 8% per annum was excessive and even award of Rs.50,000/- towards love and affection was not sustainable.
10. On other hand, Sri Hareesh S. Nayak, learned counsel for claimant submitted that though deceased was younger brother of claimant, they were residing together.
It was further submitted that claimant had sustained injury to his hand therefore, he was disable from work and was totally dependent upon deceased.
Under circumstances, assessment of tribunal towards loss of dependency was justified.
He would however claiming to be add that assessment of dependency by taking it to lower monthly income was not justified.
It was submitted that deceased was earning Rs.6,000/- per month as salary apart from Rs.100/- per day as bhatta and sought for enhancement of monthly income.

11. From above submission and since both insurer as well as claimant are questioning award on quantum, only point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether assessment of compensation by tribunal calls for modification as sought for?
12.
Insofar as dependency, claimant was examined as PW-1.
In his examination-in-chief, he stated that he was residing with deceased and since he was not able to work, deceased was supporting him.
He also relied upon Ex.P13 - survivorship certificate which indicated claimant as one of legal heirs.
However, during cross-examination PW-1 admitted that he was residing in Rajasthan and was not residing in Dharwad prior to accident.
He also admitted that he was married and had children.
13. While passing impugned award, tribunal has referred to deposition and contents of documents and concluded that deceased was supporting claimant and was maintaining family.
However, said conclusion in light of evidence referred to above would be perverse and untenable.
There is no specific evidence, apart from survivorship certificate would indicate that claimant was dependent upon deceased.
Since he had admitted that he was married and living in Rajasthan, averment of claimant have to be held as not substantiated.

Taking note of ratio laid down by Division Bench of this Court in Managing Director, KSRTC v/s Venkataramappa K.S. and Ors., reported in ILR 2002 KAR 887, wherein it held that all legal representatives are entitled to file claim petitions, it has to be held that claim petition would be maintainable.

However, compensation under such cases would have to be assessed in terms of another Division Bench of this C ourt in case of A. Manavalagan v/s A. Krishnamurthy and Ors., reported in ILR 2004 KAR 3268, where method has been evolved for assessing loss of estate substantively, at 25% of monthly income of deceased instead of The Divisional Manager vs Rajendra Singh on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74304366/
4 compensation towards loss of dependency.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. Insofar as monthly income, though claimant stated that he was earning Rs.6,000/-per month and Rs.100/- per day as bhatta, same is not substantiated.
In absence, it has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2015 is Rs.8,000/-, therefore same has to be considered.
To said amount future prospects at 40% has to be added.

Thus, loss of estate would be as follows:
25% of (Rs.8,000/- + 40% X 12 X 18) = Rs.6,04,800/-.
Rounded of Rs.6,05,000/-.
15. Apart from that claimant would be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

Thus,
claimant is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,20,000/.
16.
Tribunal has awarded interest at rate of 8% per annum.
This Court in case of Shriram General Insurance v/s Smt. Lakshmi and Ors., reported in (2018) 4 AKR 808, has stated that in case of award by claims tribunal, rate of interest has to be at 6%.

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance v/s Smt. Lakshmi and Ors., reported in (2018) 4 AKR 808
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, claimant would be entitled to interest at 6% per annum on award.
Thus, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

17. Consequently, following:
O R D E R i. MFA.no.101234/2021 filed by claimant is dismissed.
- 10 - ii. MFA.no.102738/2020 filed by insurer is allowed in part.

iii. Claimant is held entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.6,20,000/- as against Rs.7,28,000/- awarded by tribunal with interest at rate 6% per annum from date of claim petition till its deposit.
iv. Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to tribunal for payment.
v. Insurer is directed to deposit balance compensation before tribunal within six weeks.
vi. On deposit, entire compensation is ordered to be released in favour of claimant on proper identification.
